behavior_constraints: DOT node attributes must be space-separated with no space around '=': [level="<N>" workdir="<workdir>"];
hash subcommand validates spec using the same error contract as plan/list: exit 2, stderr-only error, empty stdout on failure
hash --format short (default) prints first 12 lowercase hex chars of SHA-256 followed by \n (13 bytes total)
hash --format long prints full 64 lowercase hex chars of SHA-256 followed by \n (65 bytes total)
canonical form: for each job in list walk order, emit <name>\0<workdir>\0<command>\0deps=<d1>,<d2>,...\0env=<k1>=<v1>,<k2>=<v2>,...\n with NUL byte delimiters
deps entries preserve spec-declared order; env entries sorted by key in byte order; keys/values written verbatim with no escaping
empty deps list produces 'deps=' with nothing after '='; empty env produces 'env=' with nothing after '='
empty spec ({"jobs":[]}) canonical form is empty string, SHA-256 is e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
hash does NOT support --only; passing --only is rejected as unknown flag (exit 2, non-empty stderr)
--spec missing: exit 2, non-empty error: line on stderr, empty stdout
affected_prior: renderDot (DOT attribute separator changed from comma to space)
main (subcommand dispatch must add hash routing)
entities.summary: Add a hash subcommand that prints a SHA-256 hash of a NUL-delimited canonicalized spec representation in short or long format, and fix graph --format dot to use space-separated node attributes instead of comma-separated.

instruction_head:
# jobforge hash and DOT correction

Add a new subcommand `hash`, and make one targeted correction to
`graph --format dot` output.

The binary is still built with
`go build -o /usr/local/bin/jobforge ./cmd/jobforge` and invoked as
`jobforge <subcommand> --spec <path>`.

Existing `plan`, `run`, `validate`, and `list` behavior remains unchanged.
Existing `graph` behavior is kept, except for the one correction noted below.

## Correction to `graph --format dot`

The DOT emitter currently writes node
